consensus_divergence.consensus_view: The Exchange Rates UK survey of investment banks published on 23 August 2026, taken with EUR/USD then near 1.1677, put the median forecast at approximately 1.15 for Q3 2026, around 1.165 for Q4 2026, 1.18 for both Q1 and Q2 2027, and approximately 1.20 by Q4 2027, with the central 50% of Q3 forecasts between 1.14 and 1.16 and the Q2 2027 range spanning 1.10 to 1.21. In other words, consensus expects near-term consolidation slightly below spot followed by moderate euro appreciation as 2027 develops. Separately, aggregator compilations of individual house targets circulating in 2026 place Goldman Sachs and Deutsche Bank near 1.25, J.P. Morgan and ING near 1.22, Scotiabank at 1.24, UBS at 1.20 and Nordea most bullish toward 1.28; those individual figures are undated at house level and are treated here as indicative context rather than as precise citations. On policy, consensus is essentially unanimous: OIS prices the 10 September ECB hike at approximately 97% and a further 25bp to 2.75% fully by February 2027, and Fed funds futures price the 16 September FOMC hike at roughly 58-60%.
consensus_divergence.our_view: We are marginally more constructive than consensus tactically and materially more cautious strategically, and the divergence is about the reason rather than the level. Tactically we look for 1.1700 by end-September against a Q3 consensus median of roughly 1.15 - a 200-pip divergence in the euro's favour driven by the euro-area data-surprise run and by our slightly below-consensus view on the Fed. Strategically we look for 1.1650 in six months against a consensus that reaches 1.18 by Q1 2027 - a 150-pip divergence against the euro. On policy we agree with the market on September and disagree on the terminal: we think 2.75% by February 2027 is roughly 15-25bp too high and expect the ECB to reach 2.50% and stall.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Approximately +200 pips (+1.7%) more bullish than the Q3 2026 consensus median over the tactical horizon, and approximately -150 pips (-1.3%) less bullish than the Q1 2027 consensus median over the strategic horizon. On the ECB terminal rate we are 15-25bp below market pricing. The tactical divergence is a data-flow call; the strategic divergence is a balance-of-payments call.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Consensus is underweighting two things in opposite directions. Tactically it is underweighting the euro-area data pulse: a Q3 median of 1.15 was set against a backdrop that did not yet include the German Ifo at 88.8 versus 87.2 expected, the composite PMI at 52.1 with new orders at a 40-month high, or the August country CPI upside surprises in Spain and France. Those arrived in the last ten days of August and they are precisely what took September ECB pricing to 97%. Strategically consensus is underweighting the terms-of-trade channel almost entirely. Bank forecasts reaching 1.18-1.25 by 2027 rest overwhelmingly on Federal Reserve easing rather than on anything happening in Europe, and they do not appear to discount a euro-area current-account surplus that has already fallen from 2.0% to 1.7% of GDP with the goods surplus down EUR60bn, EU gas storage at 62.99%, an effectively closed Strait of Hormuz, and Goldman's warning that December TTF may need to exceed EUR100/MWh. Consensus is also, in our view, taking the ECB's hawkishness at face value when the ECB's own negotiated wage tracker prints 2.1% for Q2 2026 against 3.2% in 2025 and its own projections have inflation back at 2.0% in 2028.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Tactically, being long the euro into and through the September event cluster captures roughly 200 pips of divergence from the consensus median, or 1.7%, with the asymmetry improved substantially by expressing it through near-dated optionality at an estimated 8th-percentile implied volatility. Strategically, being flat or short EUR/USD against a consensus that is long captures 150 pips, and being long EUR/CHF or EUR/SEK instead of EUR/USD captures the euro's genuine rate advantage while avoiding the terms-of-trade drag and collecting 225-250bp of positive carry rather than paying 137.5bp.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: The main risk to the tactical call is a hawkish 16 September FOMC that reasserts the dollar's carry advantage and validates the consensus 1.15 Q3 median, costing roughly 108 pips from spot. The main risk to the strategic call is that a durable Hormuz reopening arrives sooner than expected: TTF collapsing below EUR40/MWh would eliminate the entire terms-of-trade objection while leaving the ECB's rate advantage substantially intact, and consensus would be right for the wrong reason - the euro would reach 1.21 and we would have been cautious on a risk that resolved. We assess that path at roughly 25% probability, which is the honest measure of how wrong this strategic view can be.

cross_currency_relative_value.cleanest_bullish_expression: Long EUR/CHF is the cleanest bullish euro expression available and it is not close. It combines the widest positive carry in the set at 225bp annualised - widening to 250bp on 10 September - with the best carry-to-volatility ratio at +0.58 against 3.90% 60-day realised volatility, and with a dated, near-certain catalyst in the ECB decision against a Swiss National Bank widely expected to hold at 0.00%, with Swiss HICP at 0.7% in July giving it no reason to move. The Bund-Confederation 10-year spread at 266bp on the consistent monthly series is wider than the 225bp policy gap, meaning the term structure already prices further euro-area tightening. Positive carry earns roughly 18 pips a month at a spot of 0.93758, rising to 20 after September. The single material caveat is entry: EUR/CHF sits at the 92nd percentile of its 52-week range and is pressing the 52-week high of 0.94118, so much of the move has been collected and the reward-to-risk on fresh entry is worse than the carry alone suggests. For a cleaner entry with the same logic, EUR/NZD is the alternative: it sits at the 12th percentile of its range, the differential flips from -25bp to +25bp on 10 September - the only cross in the set that changes carry sign on the ECB decision - and the RBNZ carries 5.6% unemployment arguing for easing.
cross_currency_relative_value.cleanest_bearish_expression: Long EUR/GBP is the cleanest short-euro expression, or equivalently the worst place to be long the euro. It carries the worst risk-adjusted carry of any euro cross at -0.51, costing 150bp a year against only 2.94% 60-day realised volatility - sterling combines a high policy rate with the lowest volatility in the complex, so carry consumes more than half of one average day's 19-pip range every month. The Bund-Gilt 10-year spread at -182.6bp is the second-widest deficit in the set. If the strategic energy thesis is the concern, EUR/NOK is the more targeted short-euro vehicle: the krone carries a 200bp rate advantage and is the direct beneficiary of the same gas shock that damages the euro area, a double exposure that has driven the cross down 6.47% over twelve months, and it is the single cleanest way to express the view that Europe's energy import bill matters more than its policy rate.
cross_currency_relative_value.relative_value_pairs: Three relative-value observations follow from the dispersion in this dossier without requiring a strong directional euro view. First, long EUR/CHF against short EUR/NOK isolates the rate story from the energy story: both legs are euro-long or euro-short on the same currency, so the trade is really long the ECB's tightening cycle against long the gas shock, and it profits if the ECB delivers without the winter squeeze materialising. Second, EUR/CAD is the purest non-carry cross in the entire benchmarking set - the ECB and Bank of Canada sit at an identical 2.25% with exactly zero differential - which makes it the correct vehicle for expressing a view on euro-area versus Canadian fundamentals with no rates overlay and the second-lowest realised volatility in the complex at 3.04%; with CAD scoring -0.103 strategically in this cycle against the euro's +0.0310, a long EUR/CAD position is the most direct expression of the relative-ranking difference. Third, the extreme range percentiles argue for mean-reversion pairs rather than directional ones: EUR/SEK at the 97th percentile with a 100th close percentile against EUR/AUD at the 3rd is a 94-percentile spread within a single base currency, and shorting the stretched leg against the compressed one is a euro-neutral way to harvest that dispersion if the carry regime that created it - VIX at 14.51 and high yield at 263bp - begins to normalise.

cross_horizon_consistency.summary: The horizons diverge: tactically Bullish at conviction 2 with a net score of +0.1359 and a rank of 3 of 11, strategically Neutral at conviction 2 with a net score of +0.0310 and a rank of 4 of 11. The divergence is one notch of stance and one place of ranking, which is a mild rather than a dramatic split, and it is entirely attributable to two factor reversals of opposite sign plus one weight change.
cross_horizon_consistency.divergence_explanation: Three mechanical changes account for the entire gap. First, the framework re-weights: External Balance rises from 0.06 tactically to 0.16 strategically, so a Bearish stance that costs only -0.0348 over two to four weeks costs -0.1056 over one to six months, and Guidance rises from 0.07 to 0.12 while Inflation & Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10. That re-weighting alone converts the euro area's energy import bill from a footnote into the second-largest force in the table. Second, three factors flip stance for genuine reasons rather than weighting: Policy & Rates goes from Neutral to Bullish because a 97%-priced hike is worthless tactically but a cross-sectional re-ranking against seven of ten peers is real strategically; Inflation & Growth goes from Bullish to Neutral because a data-surprise run is a tactical asset while an energy-driven, wage-unsupported inflation overshoot is not a strategic one; and Guidance goes from Bullish to Neutral because the market has extrapolated the ECB's hawkishness to a 2.75% terminal that the ECB's own 2.1% wage tracker does not support. Third, Flows inverts: the squeeze is spent tactically at -36,352 contracts after 22,736 of covering in one week, but a residual short against an improving differential is an asymmetric strategic asset.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The inflection is dated and falls between the two horizons. The tactical view expires with the September event cluster - the ECB on 10 September and the FOMC on 16 September - after which the rate story is delivered and the euro must be paid by something else. The strategic view turns on the northern-hemisphere gas peak in November and December, when the 62.99% August storage level is physically tested, and on the 17 December ECB projections round, at which a downward revision to the 2027 and 2028 inflation paths would reprice the terminal rate lower. The window between late September and early November is the genuine no-man's-land where neither thesis has an active catalyst.
cross_horizon_consistency.catalyst_for_transition: The transition catalyst is the exhaustion of the rate story followed by the arrival of the energy story. Concretely: once the ECB has delivered on 10 September and the FOMC has resolved on 16 September, the differential is set for at least six weeks and the euro's next marginal input is the autumn gas injection season. If EU storage reaches 85% by 1 November the strategic stance should be upgraded toward Bullish; if it stalls below 75% with TTF above EUR85/MWh the strategic stance should be downgraded toward Bearish. That single storage number is the highest-information variable in the entire dossier for the strategic horizon.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Own the euro into the September cluster and lighten after it. The forward decomposition makes this explicit: at a +134.2bp annualised forward premium the one-month outright is 1.1596 against our 1.1700 expectation for a +104 pip edge, the three-month outright is 1.1622 against 1.1650 for a +28 pip edge, and the six-month outright is 1.1661 against 1.1600 for a -61 pip edge. The edge decays to zero between one and three months and turns negative by six - buy the front of the curve and sell the back. For positions that must be held across both horizons, the crosses are the answer: long EUR/CHF or EUR/NZD carries the euro's rate advantage into the strategic window while collecting positive carry rather than paying 137.5bp a year to be long EUR/USD.

1m.annualised_pct: +1.34% (positive = EUR/USD rising in forwards, i.e. the euro appreciating in forward space, which is the mechanical consequence of the euro's negative interest-rate differential to the dollar)

edge.1m: +104 pips (the forward implies 1.1596, we expect 1.1700) - the largest edge in the structure and it is long-euro, driven by the September event cluster and the euro-area data-surprise run
edge.3m: +28 pips (the forward implies 1.1622, we expect 1.1650) - the edge decays sharply as the ECB cycle completes and the energy bill begins to bind
edge.6m: -61 pips (the forward implies 1.1661, we expect 1.1600) - the edge has inverted; over six months the forward curve is MORE bullish than we are, which is the precise quantitative statement of the tactical-bullish, strategic-neutral split

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: The forward curve embeds a +134.2bp annualised premium for the euro, derived from the pipeline's futures-implied roll premium observed on 2026-08-26 over an 18.6-to-53.6-day window; these are DERIVED outrights rather than quoted forward points, and that provenance is disclosed in the Assumptions. Because that premium is close to the 137.5bp policy differential, the cross-currency basis contributes only a few basis points, which independently corroborates the benign minus-16-to-minus-20-basis-point basis reading in Factor 10. The shape of the edge is the actionable content: +104 pips at one month, +28 pips at three months, and -61 pips at six months. An investor who buys EUR/USD forward one month and sells it forward six months captures the entire structure of this dossier's view in a single expression, and does so with no directional exposure to the level of the euro. Stated the other way round: the forward market will pay you 78 pips over six months to be long the euro, and we do not think the spot market will deliver more than 17 of them.

key_catalysts.event: Euro-area flash HICP for August (consensus 3.3% headline, 2.5% core), euro-area unemployment rate (consensus 6.3%), final manufacturing PMIs and Italian Q2 GDP
key_catalysts.rationale: This is the last major data point before the ECB's quiet period and it is the release BNY identified as the critical test of hike odds. Spanish HICP at 4.5% and French at 2.7% have already printed higher, and German regional CPIs cluster at 2.6-3.0% against a 3.1% national HICP forecast, so the risk is skewed to a beat. A print at or above 3.3% cements the 97% September pricing and validates Isabel Schnabel's hawkish messaging.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - 3.3% is the consensus, so only a print above roughly 3.4% or a core above 2.6% would surprise

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Canada rate decision, RBNZ Monetary Policy Statement, Bundesbank President Nagel speaks, French government budget balance
key_catalysts.rationale: Two of the euro's peers set policy on the same day and both are expected to hold at rates below or barely above the ECB's - the Bank of Canada at an identical 2.25% and the RBNZ at 2.50%. Any dovish tilt from either widens the euro's prospective advantage, since the ECB moves eight days later. The French budget balance, previously -EUR106.8bn, is the first dated data point in the 2027 budget process.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Mostly - holds are expected at both; the French figure is not priced at all

key_catalysts.event: Euro-area final composite and services PMIs (flash 52.1 and 51.7) and euro-area producer prices (consensus +1.3% month-on-month)
key_catalysts.rationale: The final PMIs test whether August's flash improvement holds, and BNY specifically flagged the embedded price indices as the channel through which pass-through risk becomes visible to the ECB. New orders at a 40-month high in the flash is the number to watch for confirmation. A PPI print at +1.3% month-on-month would corroborate the pipeline pressure already visible in German PPI at +3.0% year-on-year.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the flash is known, so only a revision matters, but the price indices are not priced

key_catalysts.event: CFTC Commitments of Traders release, euro-area retail sales, German factory orders and ECB Chief Economist Lane speaks
key_catalysts.rationale: The CFTC print is the first read on whether the 22,736-contract covering in the week to 25 August continued or stalled, and it lands four working days before the ECB. Lane's remarks are the last significant ECB communication before the quiet period and the most likely vehicle for any late steer on the September decision. German factory orders test whether the 54.1 manufacturing PMI is order-backed.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - both the positioning print and Lane's tone are genuinely unknown

key_catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The central event of the tactical horizon. A 25bp increase to a 2.50% deposit rate is priced at approximately 97%, so the decision itself is not the catalyst - the projections are. The June baseline was 3.0% headline HICP for 2026, 2.3% for 2027 and 2.0% for 2028, and with energy at +10.0% an upward revision to 2026 and 2027 is likely and would be read hawkishly. The risk is tonal: Lagarde acknowledged in July that there is no clear evidence of second-round effects, and repeating that alongside the hike would trigger a sell-the-fact reaction.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced on the decision (approximately 97%); NOT priced on the projection revisions or on any signal about December

key_catalysts.event: German ZEW economic sentiment (previous 34.2), euro-area ZEW (previous 31.4), final French and Spanish CPI, euro-area trade balance
key_catalysts.rationale: ZEW is the most forward-looking of the euro-area sentiment surveys and the August Ifo beat at 88.8 against 87.2 suggests upside risk. A German ZEW above 40 would confirm the recovery is broadening beyond defence-driven manufacturing, which is the specific weakness identified in the strategic Inflation & Growth assessment. The trade balance is the first monthly read on whether the goods-surplus deterioration is continuing.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - no consensus was available in the calendar for either ZEW series

key_catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The single most important two-sided event in the tactical window, and the reason Policy & Rates is Neutral rather than Bullish. Fed funds futures moved from 36% to roughly 58-60% probability of a 25bp hike after Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech on 28 August, in which he said summer inflation readings do not indicate that underlying trends have meaningfully improved. Analysts remain openly divided on whether a consensus to hike exists. A hike with a hawkish SEP widens the differential beyond 162.5bp and is euro-negative; a hold read as dovish is worth 150-200 pips of euro upside.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - approximately 58-60% of a 25bp hike, leaving roughly 40% of the outcome unpriced in either direction

key_catalysts.event: Euro-area final August HICP and Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The final HICP confirms or revises the 1 September flash and rarely deviates materially. The Bank of England decision matters more for the euro: at 3.75% the BoE pays 150bp more than the ECB, and with UK CPI at 2.9% a dovish hold or a cut signal would begin narrowing the euro's worst risk-adjusted carry deficit, which stands at -0.51 on EUR/GBP.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Final HICP fully priced; a BoE hold is expected but the guidance is not priced

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting, euro-area current account (previous +EUR35.1bn) and German producer prices
key_catalysts.rationale: The euro-area current account is the highest-information release of the month for the strategic thesis - it will show whether June's EUR35.1bn beat was a one-off or whether the goods-surplus erosion from EUR342bn to EUR282bn is continuing. The Bank of Japan matters through EUR/JPY, where a hike to 1.25% would cut the euro's 125bp carry advantage by a fifth and threaten a cross that is up 7.55% over twelve months and sits at the 84th range percentile.
key_catalysts.priced_in: BoJ hold expected; the current-account figure is not priced and no forecast was available

key_catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank quarterly monetary policy assessment, Norges Bank decision with Monetary Policy Report, and Sveriges Riksbank decision with Monetary Policy Report - all on the same day
key_catalysts.rationale: Three of the euro's ten peers set policy simultaneously and all three are expected to hold: the SNB at 0.00%, with Swiss HICP at 0.7% giving it no reason to move, Norges Bank at 4.25% and the Riksbank at 1.75%. Because the ECB will have moved to 2.50% two weeks earlier, holds by all three mechanically widen the euro's advantage over the franc to 250bp and over the krona to 75bp, and narrow its deficit to the krone to 175bp. This is the day the euro's cross-sectional re-ranking becomes arithmetic.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Holds are expected at all three; the Norges Bank and Riksbank Monetary Policy Reports contain rate paths that are not priced

key_catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia Monetary Policy Board decision
key_catalysts.rationale: The RBA is expected to hold at 4.35%, the highest policy rate in the benchmarking set and a 210bp advantage over the euro even after the ECB's September move. EUR/AUD sits at the 3rd percentile of its 52-week range, so this differential is fully expressed; only an RBA easing signal, prompted by CPI falling from 3.96%, would materially help the euro's worst-performing cross.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Hold fully expected

key_catalysts.event: ECB publishes the Account of the 10 September monetary policy meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: The Account is the ECB's minutes equivalent and is released roughly four weeks after each meeting; the July Account published on 27 August moved September pricing decisively by twice describing the hold as a pause. The September Account will reveal whether the Council views 2.50% as a waypoint or a destination, and given the market prices a 2.75% terminal by February 2027 this is the most likely single source of terminal-rate repricing inside the horizon.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the Council's internal balance after delivering the hike is unknown

key_catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision, Bank of Canada decision with Monetary Policy Report, RBNZ Monetary Policy Review
key_catalysts.rationale: The second FOMC of the strategic horizon and the point at which the Warsh Federal Reserve's reaction function becomes legible. If the Fed has hiked in September, October tests whether it is a cycle or a one-off; core PCE at 3.3% argues for the former. The Bank of Canada's Monetary Policy Report is the vehicle for any move away from the 2.25% that currently matches the ECB exactly.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced this far out

key_catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision (no staff projections)
key_catalysts.rationale: A non-projection meeting six weeks after the September move. The base case is a hold at 2.50%, and the market's 2.75%-by-February pricing means the language matters more than the decision. A hold framed as another pause sustains the terminal; a hold framed as data-dependent with softening wage commentary begins the downward repricing we expect.
key_catalysts.priced_in: A hold is expected; the guidance is not priced

key_catalysts.event: Northern-hemisphere heating season begins in earnest - the physical test of the 62.99% EU gas storage level recorded on 24 August
key_catalysts.rationale: This is the highest-information event of the strategic horizon and it has no fixed date, which is why it is expressed as a week-of. EU storage at 62.99% on 24 August was well below historical averages and among the lowest ever recorded for the time of year, against an effectively closed Strait of Hormuz carrying almost a fifth of global LNG trade. Goldman Sachs has said current prices will not be enough for Europe to manage storage through winter and that December TTF may need to exceed EUR100/MWh. Every EUR10/MWh on TTF is a direct debit to the euro-area goods surplus.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced in the currency; the forward gas curve prices a difficult but manageable winter, and EUR/USD carries no visible energy discount at 1.15831

key_catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections, Bank of Canada decision, RBNZ Monetary Policy Statement
key_catalysts.rationale: The final FOMC of 2026 with a full SEP, and the point at which the Federal Reserve's 2027 dot plot becomes visible under Warsh. Consensus bank forecasts reaching EUR/USD 1.18-1.25 in 2027 rest overwhelmingly on Fed easing; a 2027 dot plot showing no cuts would remove the foundation of those forecasts and is the largest single risk to the consensus view we are diverging from.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced

key_catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff projections; Bank of England MPC; Norges Bank Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The pivotal event of the strategic horizon. This is the projections round at which energy base effects from the 2026 shock first come clearly into the 2027 and 2028 forecast window. If the staff revise the 2027 path down toward 2.0%, the market's 2.75% terminal pricing loses its justification and the strip reprices lower - the specific euro-negative repricing this dossier expects. If instead the projections show second-round effects finally appearing in the wage and services paths, the terminal holds and the strategic stance should be upgraded.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - a hold at 2.50% is the base case but the projection revisions are the unpriced content

key_catalysts.event: Expiry of the European Union's six-month pause on retaliatory tariffs against the United States
key_catalysts.rationale: The EU halted its retaliatory tariffs in early August 2026 for six months while the 15% reciprocal framework was finalised. The framework took effect on 1 July, autos were cut from 27.5% to 15% retroactive to 1 August, and the Commission tabled the EU-side regulations on 28 August - so the base case is smooth continuation. But residual tariff exposure persists, notably 50% on steel and aluminium, and the expiry is a dated point at which trade risk can re-enter the euro. Cars alone are approximately 8% of EU-US trade with the US taking 29% of EU car export value.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the market treats the trade dispute as settled

key_catalysts.event: Market-priced date by which a second ECB hike to a 2.75% deposit rate is fully discounted
key_catalysts.rationale: Not a scheduled event but a priced one, and it is the specific market expectation this dossier disagrees with. OIS has a further 25bp apparently discounted by early 2027 (flagged as unverified), against an ECB negotiated wage tracker at 2.1% for Q2 2026 versus 3.2% in 2025, and against the ECB's own June projections showing headline inflation at 2.0% in 2028. We think the terminal drifts to 2.50-2.625%. Delivery of 2.75% would validate the strategic Policy & Rates contribution of +0.1296 and argue for an upgrade; failure to deliver removes it.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced - this is precisely the pricing we are fading

key_catalysts.event: Ongoing: US-Iran conflict and the status of the Strait of Hormuz - no scheduled date, monitored continuously
key_catalysts.rationale: The highest-impact and least predictable factor in the dossier, and genuinely two-sided. On 31 August Iran's IRGC claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait and attacked a UAE air base, following Iranian strikes on US bases in Jordan - the trend is escalatory. Escalation is euro-negative through gas, terms of trade and the euro's non-haven beta. But a durable ceasefire and Hormuz reopening would collapse TTF and Brent, restore the euro-area goods surplus and remove the dollar's haven bid - net euro-positive, because the terms-of-trade channel is larger for the euro than the rate channel it would cost.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced in the volatility surface - the EUR/USD term structure is in clean contango from 5.357% at 43.6 days to 5.834% at 190.6 days with no event premium whatsoever

invalidators.condition: The 16 September FOMC hikes 25bp with a hawkish Summary of Economic Projections showing a 2027 median above 4.00%, widening the EUR-USD policy differential beyond 162.5bp
invalidators.mechanism: Policy & Rates contributes exactly zero to the tactical score precisely because the Fed leg is unresolved at 58-60%. Resolution in the hawkish direction converts that zero into a negative and simultaneously removes the foundation of the consensus 2027 forecasts that rest on Fed easing. A 162.5bp differential takes the carry cost of a long EUR/USD position from 13 to 15 pips a month against a 44-pip ATR.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Fed funds futures implied probability for September and the December 2027 SEP median dot
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily into 16 September, then at each FOMC
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: EUR-USD policy differential wider than 162.5bp, or a 2027 SEP median above 4.00%

invalidators.condition: EU gas storage fails to reach 75% by 1 November 2026 and front-month TTF closes above EUR100/MWh
invalidators.mechanism: External Balance already contributes -0.1056 of the strategic score at a 0.16 weight. Goldman Sachs has said December TTF may need to exceed EUR100/MWh if Middle East exports normalise only gradually; at that level the euro-area goods surplus, already down from EUR342bn to EUR282bn, deteriorates fast enough to push the twelve-month current account below 1.0% of GDP. That would take External Balance to a Bearish 80 confidence, worth -0.128, overwhelming the +0.1296 Policy contribution.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Aggregated Gas Storage Inventory EU fill level and ICE Dutch TTF front-month settlement
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: EU storage below 75% on 1 November, or TTF front-month above EUR100/MWh on a weekly close

invalidators.condition: The ECB hikes on 10 September and explicitly signals the tightening cycle is complete, or the 17 December projections revise the 2027 inflation path down, collapsing euro-area terminal pricing below 2.50%
invalidators.mechanism: The strategic Policy & Rates contribution of +0.1296 is the single largest positive in the dossier and it rests entirely on 50bp of further tightening being delivered rather than merely priced. If the terminal collapses to 2.50%, the euro's prospective re-ranking from eighth to sixth in the policy-rate table does not occur, its sterling deficit stays at 150bp rather than narrowing to 75bp, and the entire strategic bull case is removed at once.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Euro-area OIS terminal-rate pricing and the ECB statement language on further tightening
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Euro-area terminal-rate pricing below 2.50% at any point after 10 September

invalidators.condition: The OAT-Bund 10-year spread widens beyond 120bp during the French 2027 budget process
invalidators.mechanism: Fiscal & Sovereign Risk is currently Neutral at both horizons precisely because spreads are contained at 83.6bp on OATs and roughly 81-85bp on BTPs. A move beyond 120bp reintroduces a fragmentation premium across the whole euro complex, constrains ECB hawkishness because the Governing Council cannot tighten into a widening periphery, and would turn Factor 8 Bearish at 65 confidence, worth -0.0455 strategically. Fitch's 28 August affirmation came with an explicit warning on exactly this path.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: French 10-year OAT yield minus German 10-year Bund yield
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: OAT-Bund above 120bp on a weekly close

invalidators.condition: The euro-area flash HICP undershoots 3.0% headline on 1 September or the September composite PMI falls below 51.0
invalidators.mechanism: Inflation & Growth contributes +0.1026 of the +0.1359 tactical score - approximately 76% of the entire signal - and that contribution rests on an unbroken positive-surprise run. A headline undershoot below 3.0% against a 3.3% consensus would immediately put the 97% September hike pricing in question, and a composite PMI back below 51.0 would say the August improvement was noise. Either alone cuts the tactical score to roughly +0.05 and the stance to Neutral.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Eurostat flash HICP and the S&P Global euro-area composite PMI
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Flash HICP headline below 3.0%, or composite PMI below 51.0

invalidators.condition: A durable US-Iran ceasefire reopens the Strait of Hormuz and TTF falls below EUR40/MWh while euro-area core HICP falls below 2.2%
invalidators.mechanism: This is the invalidator that would be pleasant to be wrong about. It removes the -0.1056 External Balance drag entirely by restoring the euro-area terms of trade and the goods surplus, and simultaneously removes the dollar's haven bid. The condition includes core HICP below 2.2% deliberately: if the ECB cycle survives the energy reversal the euro gets both legs, but if core collapses with energy the Policy contribution goes too and the net effect is smaller than it first appears. On balance the terms-of-trade channel is larger and the strategic stance should be upgraded.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ICE Dutch TTF front-month, Brent crude, and Eurostat core HICP ex energy, food, alcohol and tobacco
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily on energy, monthly on inflation
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: TTF below EUR40/MWh on a monthly average with Brent below $70

invalidators.condition: CFTC non-commercial euro positioning converts to a net long above +50,000 contracts while EUR/USD holds above the 200-day moving average at 1.16335
invalidators.mechanism: Flows contributes +0.0330 strategically on the argument that a residual -36,352 short against an improving differential converts to demand. Confirmation of that conversion - roughly 86,000 contracts, or USD 12.5bn of notional at 1.15831 - alongside a decisive break of the 200-day would flip the daily moving-average stack from bearish to bullish and add systematic buying on top. Both conditions are required: positioning without the level is a crowded long, and the level without positioning is a false break.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Commitments of Traders non-commercial net position and EUR/USD daily closes versus the 200-day moving average
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly on positioning, daily on price
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Non-commercial net above +50,000 contracts with three consecutive daily closes above 1.16335

invalidators.condition: The euro-area twelve-month current-account surplus prints below 1.5% of GDP in the ECB balance-of-payments releases
invalidators.mechanism: The surplus has fallen from EUR305bn and 2.0% of GDP to EUR276bn and 1.7% over twelve months, driven by a EUR60bn fall in the goods surplus. A print below 1.5% would confirm that the energy import bill is compounding rather than stabilising and would raise External Balance confidence from 68 toward 78, taking its contribution from -0.1056 to -0.1248 and pushing the strategic net score negative on its own.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ECB euro area monthly balance of payments, twelve-month cumulated current account as a percentage of GDP
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Monthly, released roughly seven weeks after the reference month
invalidators.quantitative_threshold: Twelve-month current account below 1.5% of euro-area GDP

signposts.current_level: EU storage 62.99% full at end of gas day 24 August 2026, well below historical averages and among the lowest ever for the time of year; TTF above EUR70/MWh on 31 August 2026, the first time since January 2023

factors_changed: Factor 1 Policy & Rates: tactical stance unchanged at Neutral but confidence raised from 58 to 61, and strategic unchanged at Bullish with confidence raised from 52 to 54. The change reflects the July Account published on 27 August, which twice characterised the hold as a pause, and the move in September pricing from the 76.9-83% range recorded a month ago to approximately 97%.

Factor 3 Risk Appetite: tactical stance CHANGED from Neutral 56 to Bullish 55. The VIX has fallen from the high teens to 14.51 with a 2026 low of 14.2, the Euro Stoxx 50 set an all-time high above 6,560, and the broad dollar index fell 2.1% over the month - the goldilocks configuration the euro brief identifies as optimal for the anti-dollar has arrived since the last report.

Factor 4 Flows & Positioning: tactical stance CHANGED from Bullish 62 to Neutral 60, and strategic CHANGED from Neutral 48 to Bullish 55. This is the largest single revision in the dossier and it is entirely mechanical: the prior report recorded a leveraged-fund net short of 56,671 contracts at the 0th percentile, an extreme that has since been substantially unwound, with the non-commercial aggregate covering from -59,088 to -36,352 in the single week to 25 August. The tactical squeeze has been spent; the strategic residual has become the asymmetry.

Factor 6 Guidance & Credibility: strategic stance CHANGED from Bullish 57 to Neutral 55. The ECB's guidance has been more effective, not less - but the market has now extrapolated it to a 2.75% terminal by February 2027, and reconciling that with a negotiated wage tracker at 2.1% and the ECB's own 2.0% inflation projection for 2028 is the source of the downgrade.

Factor 8 Fiscal & Sovereign Risk: tactical stance CHANGED from Bearish 50 to Neutral 58, and strategic CHANGED from Bearish 57 to Neutral 52. Fitch affirmed France at A+ with a stable outlook on 28 August rather than acting on the warnings, peripheral spreads remain contained at 83.6bp on OATs against 81-82bp a month ago and roughly 81-85bp on BTPs, and the scale of the German fiscal expansion - new borrowing reported above EUR180bn in the adopted budget and a EUR500bn infrastructure fund - is better characterised as a growth positive than a supply negative given that spreads have not widened.

Factor 10 USD Liquidity & Funding: tactical stance CHANGED from Bullish 58 to Neutral 53, and strategic CHANGED from Bullish 55 to Neutral 53. Funding conditions have not deteriorated - the basis, credit spreads and the Fed balance sheet all remain benign - but Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech on 28 August pushed the dollar toward the US-exceptionalism side of the dollar smile, which offsets the abundant-liquidity argument that supported a Bullish reading a month ago.

Factors 2, 5, 7 and 9 retained their stances at both horizons with only minor confidence adjustments: Inflation & Growth stays Bullish tactically at 57 and moves from Neutral 50 to Neutral 55 strategically as the wage evidence firmed; External Balance stays Bearish at both horizons with strategic confidence eased to 66 on verification; Event Risk stays Bearish with strategic confidence eased from 57 to 52 as the two-sidedness of the Gulf conflict became clearer; Market Structure stays Neutral with confidence raised at both horizons.
signposts_triggered: TRIGGERED, adversely: the prior report's signpost on the Dutch TTF front-month gas price recorded EUR58.62/MWh at the 30 July close. It has since risen to above EUR70/MWh on 31 August 2026, the highest since January 2023, and EU storage at 62.99% on 24 August is materially worse than the 49-55% recorded in July only because the seasonal injection has been slower than normal. The energy signpost has moved decisively in the euro-negative direction.

TRIGGERED, favourably: the prior report's signpost on the market-implied probability of a September ECB hike recorded 76.9% to 83% at the end of July. It now sits at approximately 97%. The confirming threshold was crossed.

TRIGGERED, favourably: the prior report's signpost on CFTC leveraged-fund positioning recorded a net short of 56,671 contracts at the 0th percentile. The non-commercial aggregate has since covered to -36,352, a substantial unwind of the extreme - though this has removed the tactical squeeze rather than delivering it.

TRIGGERED, favourably: the prior report's signpost on the US 10-year minus German 10-year spread recorded +152bp to +159bp on 29-31 July. It now stands at approximately 138bp on live levels - a narrowing of roughly 15-20bp in the euro's favour, and one of the clearest confirming moves of the month.

NOT TRIGGERED: the OAT-Bund spread was 81-82bp on 30-31 July and is 83.6bp on 21 August - essentially unchanged and well inside the invalidating threshold. French fiscal risk has not yet materialised.

PARTIALLY TRIGGERED: the euro-area HICP signpost recorded 2.9% headline and 2.5% core in the July flash. The final July print confirmed both, and the August flash consensus of 3.3% headline with core unchanged at 2.5% represents an escalation in headline without corroboration in core - which is precisely the composition problem at the heart of this month's strategic Neutral.

PARTIALLY TRIGGERED: the wage tracker signpost recorded 2.3% for 2026 and 2.7% for Q1 2027 at the 29 July release. The June-dated tracker shows Q2 2026 at 2.1% against Q1 at 1.8%, with full-year 2026 at 2.3% smoothed and 2.6% unsmoothed. Wage pressure remains contained, which supports the strategic caution rather than the tactical optimism.
change_since_last_report.conviction_change: Unchanged at both horizons: tactical conviction remains 2 of 5 and strategic conviction remains 2 of 5. The underlying weighted scores softened modestly, with the tactical net falling from +0.1876 to +0.1359 and the strategic net from +0.0820 to +0.0310, but neither crossed a conviction boundary. Overall confidence rose marginally tactically, from 56 to 57, and fell marginally strategically, from 54 to 54 unchanged. The G10+SGD ranking improved at both horizons: from 4 of 11 to 3 of 11 tactically and from 6 of 11 to 4 of 11 strategically, which is the most meaningful change in the report - the euro's absolute case has softened slightly while its relative case has improved, because the ECB is now visibly tightening while most peers hold or lean toward easing.
new_catalysts: The Federal Reserve chair's Jackson Hole speech on 28 August was not a catalyst in the prior report and is now the dominant near-term two-sided risk: September FOMC hike odds moved from 36% to approximately 58-60%, which is the specific reason Policy & Rates is held at Neutral tactically rather than Bullish.

The publication of the ECB's Account of the 22-23 July meeting on 27 August, which twice described the hold as a pause, is new since the prior report and is what took September pricing from the low 80s to 97%.

The effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the 31 August escalation - the IRGC claiming it downed a US MQ-9 drone over the Strait and attacked a UAE air base - materially sharpens the energy catalyst relative to a month ago.

Goldman Sachs' assessment that current prices will not be enough for Europe to manage storage through winter, and that December TTF may need to exceed EUR100/MWh, gives the winter gas risk a quantified threshold it did not have in the prior report.

Fitch's affirmation of France at A+ with a stable outlook on 28 August, alongside an explicit warning on deficits, converts French fiscal risk from an undated concern into a dated one anchored on the 2027 budget process.

The completion of the EU-US tariff process - the Commission tabling the EU-side regulations on 28 August to enable retroactive 15% auto tariffs from 1 August - retires a risk that was live in the prior report, and introduces a new dated one in the early-February 2027 expiry of the EU's retaliation pause.
change_since_last_report.thesis_trajectory: The thesis is broadly unchanged but has become more sharply defined since 2026-08-01. A month ago the euro's case was a hawkish ECB against a soft global backdrop; today it is a hawkish ECB against a hawkish Federal Reserve, with the energy terms-of-trade drag quantified far more precisely. Both weighted scores softened - tactical from +0.1876 to +0.1359 and strategic from +0.0820 to +0.0310 - because the two things that improved for the euro, September pricing at 97% and a 15-20bp narrowing in the UST-Bund spread, were offset by two that deteriorated: the Fed turning hawkish and TTF gas rising from EUR58.62 to above EUR70/MWh against a storage level that has not caught up. The single most important change is that the tactical positioning tailwind identified a month ago has been collected rather than remaining available. In one sentence: the thesis is unchanged in direction and weaker in force, but the euro's RELATIVE standing has improved from 4th to 3rd tactically and from 6th to 4th strategically, because it is now one of very few currencies in the benchmarking set with a central bank that is actually raising rates.

seasonality.pattern: One documented euro seasonal pattern is directly relevant inside these horizons, and it is the one the euro brief identifies: the ECB's quarterly staff-projection rounds in March, June, September and December carry disproportionate weight, because changes to the growth and inflation forecast paths are the highest-signal communication the institution produces. Two of the four fall inside this dossier's windows - 10 September inside the tactical horizon and 17 December inside the strategic one - which is an unusually dense concentration and is why both syntheses are anchored on projection meetings rather than on the intervening 29 October decision. The September round matters most in the near term because it is the first opportunity to revise the June baseline of 3.0% headline HICP for 2026, 2.3% for 2027 and 2.0% for 2028 in light of an energy shock that has since intensified. The December round matters most strategically because it is the first projection vintage in which the 2026 energy base effects come clearly into the 2027 and 2028 forecast window - the specific mechanism by which we expect the market's 2.75% terminal pricing to be repriced lower. A second, milder seasonal consideration falls at the far edge of the strategic horizon: year-end portfolio rebalancing and the associated 31 December dollar-funding turn, at which dealer balance-sheet compression reliably widens cross-currency basis. With the 3-month EUR/USD basis already benign at approximately minus 16 to minus 20 basis points, that turn is a technical rather than a directional consideration this year. A third pattern that would ordinarily be listed - the northern-hemisphere heating season - is treated in this dossier as a dated fundamental catalyst rather than a seasonal one, because the 62.99% August storage level and the closed Strait of Hormuz make this winter's gas balance a specific supply event rather than a recurring annual pattern. No other euro seasonal pattern is asserted; none is fabricated.
seasonality.relevance: High for the tactical horizon and high for the strategic horizon, because the 10 September and 17 December ECB projection rounds are the two pivotal scheduled events in the dossier.

assumptions: Convention: this dossier is written from the euro's perspective and every rate quoted is EUR-first. EUR/USD is quoted as US dollars per euro, and all nine crosses (EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY, EUR/CHF, EUR/AUD, EUR/CAD, EUR/NOK, EUR/NZD, EUR/SEK, EUR/SGD) are quoted euro-first. On every pair in this dossier a RISING rate means a STRONGER euro, and "Bullish EUR" means those rates rising. There is no inverted quote anywhere in this document.

Price and analytics provenance: spot rates, moving averages, realised volatility, ATR, 52-week ranges and percentiles, support and resistance zones, and the futures-implied roll premium are read from the pipeline's gated, append-only price store and its derived per-pair analytics as of the 2026-08-28 close. Realised volatility is READ, not recomputed, so that it matches the figure the downstream pair analysis uses for the same pair on the same day. Weekend bars never enter the store, so the 252-day annualisation is correct. Where a live intraday level differs from the 2026-08-28 close - EUR/USD traded near 1.1600 on 31 August - both are stated and the close is used for all calculations.

Forward rates are DERIVED, not quoted. The 1-month, 3-month and 6-month EUR/USD outrights of 1.1596, 1.1622 and 1.1661 are computed from the pipeline's futures-implied roll premium of +134.2bp annualised, observed on 2026-08-26 over an 18.6-to-53.6-day window, applied linearly to the 1.15831 spot. That premium equals the interest-rate differential plus the cross-currency basis, not the policy differential. No quoted forward-points source was available this cycle, and any conclusion drawn from the forward decomposition should be read with that provenance in mind.

Sovereign yield methodology: the pipeline's cached 10-year sovereign series are MONTHLY and stand as of 2026-06-01. The bilateral spread table in the Rate Differentials section is computed entirely on that consistent monthly basis so that all legs are directly comparable, and every entry is labelled accordingly. Live German, French, Italian and US levels are sourced separately and quoted with their own dates wherever the current level is material - which means some cross-date comparisons appear in the text, notably the roughly 138bp UST-Bund spread that pairs a 31 August Bund with a 27 August Treasury, and the roughly 81-85bp BTP-Bund spread that pairs a 28 August BTP auction with a 31 August Bund. These are disclosed as approximations rather than presented as precise.

PPP substitution: no OECD purchasing-power-parity series exists in the pipeline cache and no free, dated PPP table could be sourced this cycle. The ten-entry valuation table therefore uses BIS real effective exchange rate levels for June 2026 to compute a relative real-valuation proxy, expressed as the percentage by which the euro's REER of 102.69 differs from each peer's. This measures real effective appreciation relative to the BIS base period and is NOT an absolute purchasing-power fair value; the deviation figures should not be read as implied equilibrium exchange rates. The substitution is disclosed rather than hidden and is recorded as a documented gap in the run log.

CFTC taxonomy: two different CFTC datasets appear in this dossier and they are not interchangeable. The -36,352 figure is the NON-COMMERCIAL net position from the legacy Commitments of Traders report dated 25 August 2026, sourced through research. The -60,600 leveraged-fund and +225,389 asset-manager figures are from the Traders in Financial Futures report and are the pipeline's latest cached tranche dated 11 August 2026, which is 21 days stale at the valuation date. Because the aggregate has covered materially since 11 August, leveraged funds are almost certainly less short than the cached tranche shows. Both figures are labelled with their taxonomy and date at every point of use.

Percentile estimates: three percentile figures in this dossier are ESTIMATES rather than published values and are labelled as such wherever they appear. The BIS REER historical percentile of 45 is estimated against the cached cross-sectional and time-series window. The CFTC net-position percentile of 30 is estimated against the trailing year. The EUR/USD implied-volatility percentile of 8 is estimated by comparing the current 43.6-day CME at-the-money level of 5.357% against a May-2026 market reference that placed the 2026 low at 5.4%; no clean one-year implied-volatility history was sourceable.

Central-bank meeting dates are taken exclusively from the pipeline's calendar file, which is authoritative for scheduled decisions and is never web-searched. This matters because web sources encountered during research gave incorrect September dates for the Bank of England and the Riksbank; the calendar dates of 17 September and 24 September respectively are used. Singapore is absent from that calendar by design, because the Monetary Authority of Singapore operates an S$NEER policy band rather than a policy rate, and this dossier does not impute one.

Macro table substitutions: three cached CPI vintages were stale at the valuation date - Switzerland, Norway and Sweden were all carried at 2025-Q4 values - and have been replaced with the July 2026 HICP prints published in the Eurostat release of 19 August 2026 (0.7%, 2.9% and 0.3% respectively). The US headline CPI has likewise been replaced with the 3.4% July monthly print rather than the 3.863% cached 2026-Q2 quarterly average. Every substitution is noted in the table itself. Where no reliable figure existed - Japanese CPI, every Singapore field, and seven of eleven preferred-core measures - the cell is recorded as a documented gap and is NOT estimated.

Stale and missing data explicitly flagged: the 3-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis of approximately minus 16 to minus 20 basis points dates from mid-May 2026 and is 3.5 months old; the 3-month JPY/USD basis, the Federal Reserve's monthly QT cap, the 25-delta 1-month EUR/USD risk reversal, Citi economic surprise index values, FXE and EUO ETF flows, Target2 balances, euro-area sovereign CDS quotes and any ECB voting split could not be sourced and are recorded as gaps. No figure has been substituted for any of them. In particular, no directional inference is drawn anywhere in this dossier from the options skew, because the risk reversal is a gap.

Tail-risk probabilities in the Event Risk factor and the scenario probabilities in both syntheses are the author's structured estimates, not sourced market-implied figures. They are internally consistent - each scenario set sums to 100% - but they are judgements and should be treated as such.

Cache data-quality disclosure carried forward: the pipeline flagged that only two EUR/USD resistance zones met its two-touch threshold against nine support zones. The resistance levels in this dossier are therefore supplemented with the 200-day moving average at 1.16335 and the 1.1700 round number, and the shortfall is disclosed rather than concealed. The same shortfall was flagged for EUR/CAD, EUR/JPY, EUR/NOK and EUR/NZD.

Implied volatility provenance: EUR/USD is the only euro pair with a genuine quoted implied-volatility curve in the cache, sourced from CME at-the-money options and observed on 2026-08-26. The implied volatilities cached for EUR/AUD, EUR/CAD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP, EUR/JPY and EUR/NZD are triangle-realised-correlation ESTIMATES rather than quotes, because no listed option exists on those crosses, and EUR/NOK, EUR/SEK and EUR/SGD have no cached implied volatility at all. Only the EUR/USD curve is used for any analytical conclusion in this dossier.

Adversarial verification pass (Phase 6), applied 2026-09-01: an independent fact-checking agent re-checked 21 headline claims against their cited primary sources and swept all 40 citation URLs. Corrections applied: euro-area energy HICP was corrected from +10.3% to +10.0% year-on-year; the Federal Reserve balance-sheet figure was corrected to $6.75 trillion with a year-on-year change of approximately +1.7% rather than an arithmetically impossible +0.3%; the TTF gas level was updated to above EUR70/MWh on 31 August, the first time since January 2023; the claim that the United States retains tariffs on roughly 70% of EU exports was WITHDRAWN as pre-dating the July 2026 framework and unsupported by the cited source; the euro-area composite PMI was reframed as a flash reading of 52.1 against a 52.0 prior rather than a beat against a 51.7 consensus, because 51.7 is the services index; the German 2026 budget figures were split between the citable July 2025 draft and the adopted-budget figures reported elsewhere, with the discrepancy disclosed; a Reuters SNB economist poll citation was withdrawn because it was dated September 2025 and referred to the 2025 meeting, and the SNB hold expectation is now an inference from Swiss HICP at 0.7% rather than a sourced survey; the CFTC prior-week figure was corrected from -59,100 to -59,088; the Federal Reserve H.4.1 citation was repointed from the rolling 'current' URL to the dated 20 August 2026 release; and the BIS citation was repointed to the statistics portal, with an explicit note that the 102.69 REER level is cache-sourced and could not be reproduced from the BIS landing page. Staleness now labelled in-text: BIS REER (92 days), ECB wage tracker (76 days), the German budget citation (398 days) and the cross-currency basis (3.5 months). Confidence was LOWERED on the five affected factors as a result - Factor 1 from 63/56 to 61/54, Factor 2 from 60/58 to 57/55, Factor 5 from 60/68 to 58/66, Factor 8 from 60/55 to 58/52 and Factor 10 from 56/55 to 53/53 - which moved the tactical net score from +0.1401 to +0.1359 and the strategic net from +0.0326 to +0.0310. Neither stance nor conviction nor G10 rank changed at either horizon.
